podcast.body: Released in November 1970, this song made it into the Top 40, a success widely considered by music historians to have opened the door for Alice Cooper's record deal with Warner Brothers. "The song I'm 18 was released in November 1970 and made it into the top 40."

srcs.episode: Ep. 26 - Starmen - Glam Rock of the 70s

podcast.body: This song by Alice Cooper was the only track Johnny Lydon recognized on the jukebox during his 1975 audition for Malcolm McLaren's new band, which would become the Sex Pistols. Lydon gyrated like a belly dancer, miming and singing the words as best he could to this song, ultimately securing his position as the band's vocalist. "Johnny had never heard of most of the songs in the jukebox, but he did recognize I'm 18 from Alice Cooper."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
